title: Takeoff Distance Over a 50 Ft Obstacle
conditions: Wing flaps 15°, paved/level/dry runway, full throttle and max RPM, attain 91 MPH at 50 ft AGL

exampleCheck.note: Worked example printed on the chart (points A-F). Re-measured directly from reference/fig5-07-takeoff-distance-50ft.png pixel positions on 2026-10-01, superseding an earlier pass that had the right-axis calibration correct but (a) misidentified which curve point A sits on during automated tracing, giving a wrong B value, and (b) never independently verified the example's own weight/wind inputs, inheriting an assumed oatF=65/weightLb=3100/windMph=10 from a sibling chart. Correct example inputs, read directly off the dashed line's axis crossings: oatF=70 (not 65), weight=3200 (not 3100), wind=30mph headwind (not 10) -- the same wind=30 pattern confirmed on fig5-06 and fig5-08, and a windKPerMph (0.0055) that matches fig5-06's independently-derived value almost exactly, which is a strong cross-chart consistency check. Measured B=2994 ft, D=2776 ft, F=2318 ft; weightExponent and windKPerMph refit from these. Model reproduces the worked example to within 0.02%.

unverifiedAltitudes.note: The 0/2000/4000/8000 ft altitudeCurves entries below are the ORIGINAL, unverified digitization. Only the 6000 ft entry (above) and the weight/wind exponents have been independently re-measured pixel-by-pixel against the source chart. A reliable automated trace of the other four curves was not achieved in this pass — they cross near a steep 'STD TEMP' reference line on the chart that repeatedly caused the curve-tracer to jump between curves, and disambiguating each one visually would need more time than this pass allowed. These others likely carry similar error and should be re-checked before being trusted for altitudes other than 6000 ft.
